title: Gamjatang
subtitle: korean pork and vegetable spicy soup
excerpt: Gamjatang is a thick, deeply spiced Korean soup made from pork, perilla, mushrooms, and spring onion in a rich, red chilli broth. It is a hearty, warming dish well suited to cold weather. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Gamjatang is a traditional Korean pork soup. The name is often translated as pork spine soup. This home version uses pork belly for accessibility while keeping the flavour profile of the original.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked soup without the spring onion for up to 2 months.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the quantity easily. The flavour improves the next day.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made a day ahead and reheated.

glossaryTerms.definition: Korean red chilli flakes. They are coarser than European chilli flakes and have a fruity, mildly smoky heat. They give Korean stews and soups their characteristic red colour.
A Korean fermented soybean paste. It is saltier and stronger in flavour than Japanese miso and is used to add depth to soups and stews.

content.text: Gamjatang is built on a long-simmered pork broth coloured deep red with
chilli flakes. The pork becomes very tender with extended cooking. Serves 4 with steamed rice.

Blanch the pork in boiling water for 5 minutes to remove impurities. Drain and rinse under cold water. This step gives a cleaner, clearer broth.
Put the pork in a stockpot with the water, onion, half the garlic, and the ginger. Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook for 45 minutes.
Mix the chilli flakes, gochujang, miso paste, soy sauce, and remaining garlic to a paste. Stir into the broth.
Add the carrot and mushrooms. Simmer for a further 30 minutes until the pork is very tender and the broth is deeply flavoured. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Add the spring onion. Drizzle sesame oil over the top. Serve in deep bowls with steamed rice.

attrs.fix: Do not skip the blanching step. Rinse the pork thoroughly under cold water before adding it to the pot.

attrs.issue: Pork is still tough after 1 hour
attrs.fix: Continue simmering for a further 30 minutes. Pork belly can vary. The meat should pull apart easily when done.
Add another tablespoon of gochujang and simmer for 5 more minutes. Chilli flakes add heat but gochujang adds both heat and depth.

content.text: Gamjatang is popular at late-night restaurants in Korea, especially near university areas. It is eaten after drinking or as a warming meal in cold weather. The soup is served bubbling at the table. Diners eat it with rice and side dishes. It is a dish associated with long, slow cooking and generous portions.
